newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt mkts end steady ahead of RBNZ statement.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt mkts end steady ahead of RBNZ statement.

text.p: New Zealand debt securities ended unchanged on Monday as the market steadied itself for the Reserve Bank's six-monthly Monetary Policy Statement (MPS), to be released at 9.00 a.m. (2000 GMT) on Tuesday.
Bills and bonds were bought at the open in line with the U.S. rally on Friday, but selling soon saw yields fall back to their Friday closing levels.
"A little bit of weakness on the day. It opened up a little bit stronger on the States and also the TWI, which was about 25 points stronger," said a dealer.
The New Zealand dollar's Trade-Weighted Index strengthed this morning before falling back to close at 66.76.

Dealers said the market had rallied a long way since the formation of a centre-right coalition government last Tuesday, and investors were taking a little profit ahead of the Tuesday's key statement from the central bank.

"The consensus seems to be at least a confirmation (from the bank) of the recent moves in the short rates to the more extreme, which is that there's going to be a more explicit easing still, with an increase in the cash target and a further fall in the cash and bill rates," one dealer said.
Comments from bank Governor Don Brash on the new government's spending plans and how the bank intends to deal with its new inflation and growth targets will be a major focus for the market.

Attention will also be on the assumptions for the Trade-Weighted Index and for 90-day bank bills. A survey of economists expects the bank's forecasts to assume 90-day bank bills at 8.50 percent and the TWI at 66.10 in the first quarter of next year.
Dealers said offshore investor interest had cooled.
"Most investors are going to see how it all settles down before they get too active. If anything they're probably more net sellers in the long bond and net buyers in the shorter end," a dealer said.
